name: Build and use artifact

on:
  push:
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Produce build output
        run: |
          mkdir -p dist
          echo "Built from ${GITHUB_SHA} at $(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" > dist/build-info.txt
          echo "hello from the build job" > dist/output.txt

      - name: Upload artifact
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: build-output
          path: dist/
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 1

  consume:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # `needs` makes this job wait for `build` to finish successfully,
    # which guarantees the artifact exists before we try to download it.
    needs: build
    steps:
      - name: Download artifact
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: build-output
          path: dist/

      - name: Use artifact
        run: |
          ls -la dist/
          cat dist/build-info.txt
          cat dist/output.txt

content.text:
I added `.github/workflows/build-and-use-artifact.yml`. The repo was empty, so the build step is a placeholder that writes two text files into `dist/`. The YAML parses cleanly. I haven't run it on GitHub and haven't committed it.

**How it works:**
- **`build` job:** writes the files into `dist/` and uploads them with `actions/upload-artifact@v4` under the name `build-output`. It fails if no files are found and keeps the artifact for 1 day.
- **`consume` job:** has `needs: build`, so it only starts after `build` succeeds. That guarantees the artifact exists before it tries to fetch it. It then downloads the artifact with `actions/download-artifact@v4` into `dist/` and reads the files.

**Things to know:**
- The `name:` in the upload and download steps must match exactly. An artifact can only be uploaded once per name per run in v4, so jobs running in parallel (e.g. a matrix) each need a unique name. You can then download them all with `pattern: build-output-*` and `merge-multiple: true`.
- Jobs run on separate machines, so the artifact is the only thing passed between them. The `consume` job doesn't check out the code; add `actions/checkout@v4` if it needs repo files.
- To fit your project, replace the "Produce build output" step with your real build and point `path:` at its output folder.

The workflow runs on push, on pull requests and manually (`workflow_dispatch`). Change the `on:` section to change that.
